Hi Neha,

Thanks for the details and the form — we can definitely help get CloudScale across the finish line. At a high level, to move a Managed SaaS offer through technical validation you will need:

1) Verified Publisher account (identity + tax profile) — typically 3-5 business days after submission.
2) Offer manifest (ARM/Publisher manifest) with plan definitions and marketplace URLs.
3) A test tenancy or demo subscription and an admin test account we can use for validation.
4) Compliance info (data residency statement) and a point of contact for security questions.
5) If you want Co-sell: partner must opt in via the Partner Center and provide a co-sell MOU (DocuSign link below).

We recommend submitting the offer with a minimal plan and a working demo endpoint to speed validation. Once submitted, validation typically takes 5-10 business days depending on queue.

DocuSign for co-sell MOU: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?f=ABC123
Publishing portal (offer submit): https://partner.microsoft.com/dashboard/commerce/marketplace/offer/submit/

If useful, we can schedule a short technical triage with our validation engineer and your lead engineer. When's your team available next week?

Regards,
Azure Publisher Support
azure-publisher-support@microsoft.com

Following up with the technical checklist I've assembled for CloudScale (attached azure_offer_manifest.yaml). Highlights:
- Offer manifest must include planId, offerId, SaaS webhook URL for provisioning, and sample telemetry endpoints.
- Provide a test subscription with an admin API key and a sample prompt set (we'll publish a trimmed eval harness for validation).
- If the offer uses client-side inference or a hybrid flow, flag it in the manifest (we'll include runbooks for expected auth flows).

Markus — can you confirm whether the validation team needs load testing or just functional integration for initial certification? If load testing is needed, we can provide a scripted smoke test window.
